correctness.rationale: Adjacent vertices share the unique order-p subgroup of their cyclic subgroups, while vertices sharing it have a common prime-order neighbor, so those fibers are exactly the components and the prime-order elements are universal there. Odd p gives two adjacent universal vertices per component. For p=2 the component is nontrivial exactly when the involution has an order-four square root; otherwise it is isolated. Thus two vertices per nontrivial component are necessary and sufficient and form a perfect matching.

final_claim: For a finite p-group, total and paired domination of the proper power graph both equal twice the number of order-p subgroups when p is odd; for p=2 they exist exactly when every involution is a square, then have the same value, and every minimum total dominating set is paired.
scientific_limitations: For odd p the numerical doubling is a short deduction from known component structure; the novelty-bearing part is mainly the p=2 boundary and minimum-set behavior.
Groups with multiple prime divisors are outside this component formula.
